questions.prompt: Which of these prompts is most likely to create a compliance or privacy problem when typed into a free public AI chatbot?
choices: Rewrite this paragraph to be more concise
What are three ways to structure a project kickoff meeting?
Here is the full support ticket from customer Jane Smith (Account #48291): summarize the issue
Explain the difference between a fixed and variable cost
questions.explanation: Pasting a customer's name, account number, and support details into a public AI tool exposes personally identifiable information outside your organization's environment, which can violate privacy regulations and company policy.

questions.prompt: A colleague argues that pasting source code into a public AI tool is fine because 'it's just asking for help with a bug.' What is the main risk they are overlooking?
choices: The AI will misread the code and introduce new bugs
Proprietary source code — especially code with embedded credentials or trade secrets — may violate employment agreements or security policy when sent to a third-party service
The AI cannot read code at all
Source code is always public information if it has been compiled
questions.explanation: Proprietary source code, particularly code containing API keys, credentials, or business-sensitive logic, should not be pasted into public AI tools. This may breach employment agreements, security policies, or expose secrets.

questions.prompt: You need AI help drafting a difficult message to a client about a contract delay. The client's name and contract details are sensitive. What is the right approach?
choices: Skip using AI entirely — any task involving a client is off-limits
Paste the full contract including names and terms; the AI needs all the context to help well
Describe the situation in general terms, omitting the client's name and specific contract details
Only use the AI if you delete the conversation immediately after
questions.explanation: You can get useful help by describing the situation generically — 'a client whose project is delayed due to a vendor issue' — without exposing names, contract terms, or identifying details.
